description: Federal Crowdsourcing and Citizen Science Toolkit is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by CitizenScience.gov. Citizen science and crowdsourcing can help you engage the public in your work and collect data that might otherwise be beyond your reach. The practices can help federal agencies and other groups to innovate, collaborate, and discover new solutions. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Air Quality, Changing Seasons, Drought, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – Coastal, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Water Quality, Wildfire. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Cultural and Community Services, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
